prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts the camera wearer looking steeply downward at their own torso (brightest white at 0.1–0.3 m at the bottom edge), extended left and right arms holding hedge shears (light grey at 0.3–0.6 m in front and below the head), a rounded bush directly ahead and below (medium grey at roughly 0.6–1.2 m), a smaller bush to the left (about 1.2–1.6 m away), and the lawn, walkway, and brick house wall receding behind and below the shrubs (dark grey to black at 1.5–3.0 m). No other people are present in the scene; the camera wearer faces downward toward the top of the main shrub, keeping both hands, the shears, and the upper foliage well within arm's reach while the wearer's lower body and the rest of the house are out of view beyond the frame edges. Across the 5 frames, the hands and shear handles move laterally toward each other from roughly 0.25 m apart in frames 1–3 to nearly touching (<0.05 m apart) in frames 4–5 as the blades close and push slightly deeper into the bush cleft. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the 3D hemispherical volume of the foreground bush and the elevated height of the arms from the flat ground plane beneath them, which otherwise blend together in colour and texture. However, the map is unreliable along the thin metallic shear blades in frames 4 and 5, where the tips inserted into the foliage lose depth contrast and merge into the surrounding shrub surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's visible lower chest, shoulders, and both arms at the bottom of the frame (0.1–0.5 m from the viewpoint) as a 'person' mask, and in frame 1 segments the handheld hedge shears (0.4–0.8 m ahead and within immediate grasp) above the hands while leaving the bushes, lawn, and house wall unsegmented in black. Across the 5 frames, the left and right forearm segments converge horizontally from about 0.25 m apart in frames 1–3 until the hands meet near the bottom-centre in frames 4 and 5, while the torso remains at the bottom edge facing forward and downward with the rest of the wearer's body cropped out of view. Unlike the RGB image where the grey shirt and sunlit skin blend visually with the bright ground and silver tool handles, the segmentation map provides crisp boundary contours for the wearer's upper-body silhouette and the gap between the two arms. However, the map is highly unreliable for object recognition and temporal consistency: it mislabels the hedge shears as a 'tennis racket' in frame 1 and fails to detect them entirely in frames 2–5, where the blades are partially occluded by the bush. Additionally, in frame 2 it erroneously splits the camera wearer's own body into two separate 'person' instances (left arm in pink, right arm and torso in brown) and misses the lower handle extensions gripped beneath the hands.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only two magenta 3D hand skeletons in the lower-middle region of each frame (approximately 0.4–0.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer's head), with no yellow body skeleton detected for the wearer's visible torso and arms and no other people in the scene. Both hands are within arm's reach, positioned to the left and right of the central bush cleft, oriented forward and angled slightly inward toward each other with palms facing inward around the unrendered shear handles. Across the 5 frames, the distance between the left and right hand skeletons decreases from roughly 0.25 m in frames 1 and 2, widens slightly and shifts upward in frame 3, and then closes sharply in frames 4 and 5 until the fingers of both hands are less than 0.05 m apart and partially overlapping in frame 5. This skeletal view reveals exact finger joint articulations and the curled grip configuration of the thumbs and fingers, even for digits curled underneath the handles that are self-occluded by the backs of the hands in the RGB strip. The map is unreliable in omitting the entire upper-body skeleton despite the shoulders, chest, and forearms being clearly visible at the bottom of the frame, and in frame 5 the close proximity of the two hands causes the right and left finger keypoints to crowd together ambiguously.
